draft.title: Flow networks
card: A flow network is a directed network, so each edge has an arrow showing the way flow can go. Flow might be cars on roads, water in pipes or data in cables.
the vertex where the flow starts. Nothing flows into it along the network.
the vertex where the flow ends. Nothing flows out of it along the network.
Each edge has a capacity, the most it can carry in a set time, such as 40 cars an hour. The flow along an edge can be anything from 0 up to its capacity, and only in the direction of the arrow.
draft.remember: A flow network has arrows, a source, a sink and a capacity on every edge.

a.q: In a flow network of roads, an edge from P to Q is labelled 40. What does this mean?
opts: Up to 40 cars an hour can travel from P to Q
Exactly 40 cars an hour must travel from P to Q
Up to 40 cars an hour can travel either way
The road from P to Q is 40 kilometres long
a.why: The label is the capacity, the most the edge can carry in a set time, and the arrow gives the direction. Exactly 40 is wrong because the flow can be anything from 0 up to the capacity.
a.clue: Capacity is a limit on the flow, in one direction.

b.q: Water moves through pipes from a dam (D) to a town (T). A pipe from D to R has capacity 12 litres a second, and a pipe from R to T has capacity 9 litres a second. What is the most water that can flow from D to T along this route?
opts: 9 litres a second
12 litres a second
21 litres a second
3 litres a second
b.why: All the water must pass through both pipes in turn, so the smaller capacity of 9 limits it. Adding them to get 21 is wrong because the pipes are in a line, not side by side.
b.clue: Water must get through both pipes, one after the other.

a.best: Up to 40 cars an hour can travel from P to Q

problems.detail: The card never says that flow into a vertex must equal flow out, or that a route is limited by its smallest capacity. Finding the most a two-pipe route can carry is really the bottleneck idea from point 4 (Flow in practice), so this question asks for more than this card teaches.

a.q: In a flow network of roads, an edge from P to Q is labelled 40. What does this mean?
opts: Up to 40 cars an hour can travel from P to Q
Exactly 40 cars an hour must travel from P to Q
Up to 40 cars an hour can travel either way
The road from P to Q is 40 kilometres long
a.why: The label is the capacity, the most the edge can carry in a set time, and the arrow gives the direction. Exactly 40 is wrong because the flow can be anything from 0 up to the capacity.
a.clue: Capacity is a limit on the flow, in one direction.

b.q: A flow network of pipes has one source and one sink. Every arrow at vertex W points away from W, and every arrow at vertex K points towards K. Which is correct?
opts: W is the source and K is the sink
K is the source and W is the sink
W and K are both sinks
W and K are both sources
b.why: Nothing flows into W, so flow can only start there, which makes W the source. Nothing flows out of K, so flow ends there, which makes K the sink. Swapping them is wrong because the source is where arrows leave, not where they arrive.
b.clue: Flow starts where nothing comes in.

a.best: Up to 40 cars an hour can travel from P to Q

b.best: W is the source and K is the sink
